PullRequest.Title: Fix sandbox bypass after session disable
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #338782

Skips a redundant SDK `disableForSession` call when a queued sandbox configuration update has already disabled the session. The pending bypass is approved once instead of being rejected by the SDK's `sandbox is already disabled` error.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user disables sandboxing while an SDK sandbox-bypass permission is pending, then chooses the session-wide allow option before the configuration update finishes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The session-config event queues and awaits the existing SDK session.options.update RPC. The permission response queues behind it on the same per-session Sequencer. After the RPC publishes enabled=false, the changed callback performs one in-memory session-state read and immediately resolves the permission; this work is on the permission request's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one existing RPC for the configuration-change event in this race.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same configuration update RPC ran before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It must finish before the queued permission callback can progress because both operations share the Sequencer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the PR, one redundant RPC was attempted for the queued permission after the preceding configuration RPC had already disabled sandboxing; after the PR, zero are attempted when local state is false.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The pre-diff callback always attempted this RPC after reaching the head of the queue, even when the preceding operation had already disabled the sandbox.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Before the PR this second RPC delayed and then rejected permission resolution; the new local check removes it from the critical path in this race.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One queued callback per user-approved pending bypass request. Requests are serialized per session; once the authoritative state is false, each queued callback performs a constant-time local lookup and no additional SDK RPC.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single per-session Sequencer permits one sandbox configuration operation at a time. The configuration update runs first; queued bypass callbacks then run serially, with no burst across this session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The sandbox-enabled value is authoritative in-memory session metadata rather than a remote cache. A stored false value takes the new fast path; undefined or true preserves the prior disableForSession path. There is no negative-cache retry or invalidation change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the shared Sequencer, state publication after options.update, new false-state branch, and test assertion of zero disable requests establish the exact before/after path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK RPC duration and prevalence of this narrow user race are not measured, but the boundary count and ordering are explicit in the implementation and test.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff removes repeated IPC and shortens the permission critical path; its added work is one bounded in-memory lookup.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user approves a session-wide sandbox bypass while sandboxing remains enabled and no concurrent configuration update disables it.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The permission callback enters the per-session sandbox Sequencer, performs the added in-memory state check, then awaits the existing disableForSession SDK RPC and updates local configuration/diagnostics exactly as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per explicit allow-session approval, unchanged from before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One disableForSession RPC was issued for the approval, the same as after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The RPC remains on the permission approval critical path in the normal enabled case.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One operation per explicit session-wide bypass approval. There is no collection iteration, history growth, or per-item fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sandbox changes remain serialized to one operation per session. The diff does not increase cross-session or aggregate concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: When the authoritative state is true or absent, the new check is a miss and execution follows the unchanged RPC path. Successful state publication and lifecycle are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new branch is bypassed unless state is exactly false, leaving the existing call path intact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The RPC's absolute latency is not measured, but its unchanged cardinality and scheduling are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only added cost is one constant-time local state read before an unchanged IPC call.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced both the queued config-disable race and normal session-wide bypass flow. The production change removes a redundant serialized SDK RPC in the race and adds only a bounded in-memory state lookup elsewhere; the test adds no product-path cost. No performance finding or regression-fix learning record is warranted because the PR's demonstrated symptom is functional rejection rather than an evidenced shipped performance regression.
